patch.objective: Call another service with fetch, check response.ok, and set a timeout with AbortSignal

sources.cite: Using the Fetch API, MDN Web Docs (last modified 2025-08-20)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16. Relevant text: 'The promise returned by fetch() will reject on some errors, such as a network error or a bad scheme. However, if the server responds with an error like 404, then fetch() fulfills with a Response, so we have to check the status before we can read the response body'; 'A common pattern is to check the value of ok and throw if it is false'; json() 'will throw an exception if the response body is not in the appropriate format'.

sources.cite: Response: ok property, MDN Web Docs (last modified 2025-03-13)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16. Relevant text: ok 'contains a Boolean stating whether the response was successful (status in the range 200-299) or not'.

sources.cite: AbortSignal: timeout() static method, MDN Web Docs (last modified 2026-09-01)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16. Relevant text: it 'returns an AbortSignal that will automatically abort after a specified time'; 'The signal will abort with its AbortSignal.reason property set to a TimeoutError DOMException on timeout'; the example passes { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) } to fetch and checks err.name === "TimeoutError".

sources.cite: TypeScript & Node.js Programming Coach course outline (seed: backend/supabase/seed/tracks), objective 'Call another service with fetch, check response.ok, and set a timeout with AbortSignal'
sources.note: This band moves the JAVASCRIPT rate-board case to the TSNODE objective: the same fetch, ok check and AbortSignal.timeout, in the board's server-side proxy. Node.js's global fetch follows the same Fetch standard as the MDN pages above; the Node.js documentation itself was not re-read for this band (the TSNODE course's own Node.js sources were read for REQ-267).

brief.situation: You maintain the small Node.js proxy (rates.ts, TypeScript) that the teller rate board at Lakeside Credit Union (fictional) calls for today's rates; the proxy fetches them from the internal rate service. Since 09:10 the service has been degraded, and twice this morning a branch board showed a 30-year fixed rate of 0.00%. The next deploy train leaves at 11:00. It is 10:15.
handover: The proxy's error log is clean: whatever is going wrong is not being logged.

network.label: Read the proxy's outbound request log

console.label: Log the swallowed error in the catch and replay a request

data.workspace: rates.ts in the rate board's Node.js proxy (Lakeside Credit Union, fictional)

lines.text: const res = await fetch(RATES_URL, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) });
lastGood = { rates: data.rates, at: new Date() };
